cases.description: Auto-only control: unequal preferred main sizes, weighted growth, asymmetric padding/borders, and axis-specific gaps exercise layout without any Percent branch to mutate.
Point-only control: zero and unequal positive point bases remain intact when only Percent resolves as Auto; weighted growth and axis-specific gaps must therefore preserve every rectangle.

A zero Percent basis must replace a nonzero preferred main size, not fall back to Auto. Point and Auto siblings, no flexing, and nonzero gaps leave that zero-sized child and sibling offsets observable.

Distinct binary-exact fractional Percent bases resolve against the definite inner main size after asymmetric padding/borders. With no flexing or limits, replacing them with the unrelated preferred sizes changes the child rectangles.
A 100% basis consumes the inner main size before sibling bases and gaps; shrink is disabled so overflow cannot hide the distinction from the much smaller Auto preferred size.

A Percent ratio above one is valid and must not be clamped. The overfull first basis, a fractional Percent sibling, and a point sibling deliberately overflow without shrink, exposing Percent-as-Auto mutation.

Mixed Percent, point, and Auto bases feed unequal grow factors. The Percent preferred size differs from its resolved basis, so distributing positive free space cannot preserve all three child sizes under the mutation.

Two Percent bases and one point basis overflow the definite inner main size. Unequal scaled shrink weights operate in both normal and Percent-as-Auto layouts, with nonproportional bases ensuring different child rectangles.

One Percent main basis hits a minimum and another a maximum while a third remains unsaturated and mutation-sensitive. Cross-axis Auto/stretch, minimum, and maximum limits exercise the complete child rectangles independently.

Percent bases plus the main gap force two flex lines, while the smaller Auto preferred sizes fit one. Nonzero cross gap and space-between line distribution expose line assignment as well as child main sizes.

Unequal binary-exact Percent bases form two reversed cross-axis lines but their Auto preferred sizes fit one. Centered line distribution, distinct cross gaps, and flow-relative self alignment keep reverse flow observable.

Intentionally non-binary Percent ratios combine with fractional root edges, child dimensions, padding, borders, and gaps. Centered free space preserves a large mutation signal while complete bounds exercise edge rounding at every scale.
